category: Figure Matrix (Class A vs Class B Concentric Geometry)
question_text: Class A contains figures where a shape is nested inside an IDENTICAL larger shape. Class B contains figures where a shape is nested inside a DIFFERENT larger shape. Which option belongs to Class A?

reference_figures.label: Class A Example
reference_figures.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 100 100'><circle cx='50' cy='50' r='40' fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-width='4'/><circle cx='50' cy='50' r='15' fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-width='4'/></svg>

reference_figures.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 100 100'><rect x='20' y='20' width='60' height='60' fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-width='4'/><circle cx='50' cy='50' r='15' fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-width='4'/></svg>

options.label: A

options.label: B

explanation: Class A specifically requires the inner and outer shapes to share the same geometric class (homogenous nesting). Option A displays a small triangle perfectly nested inside a larger triangle.
